extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers learning algebraic geometry (Noetherian schemes, varieties)
extracted.subtask_description: This page is an excerpt from a textbook chapter on dimension theory for schemes and varieties: it states core theorems (Krull's Principal Ideal Theorem, Krull Height Theorem, Algebraic Hartogs), gives important exercises (about hypersurfaces, lines, fibers), and proves facts about fibers, codimension, and systems of parameters. The material is aimed at building and using technical dimension-theoretic tools in algebraic geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality of local dimension notions (Exercise 12.2.L)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose p is a closed point of a locally finite type k-scheme X. Show that the following three integers are the same: (i) dim_X p; (ii) dim O_{X,p}; and (iii) codim_X p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References Exercise 12.2.K. This identifies three a priori different notions of 'local dimension' at a closed point on a finite type k-scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dimension preserved by field extension (Exercise 12.2.M)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a locally finite type k-scheme of pure dimension n, and K/k is any field extension, then X_K has pure dimension n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: reduce to affine X = Spec A, then to A integral. Write K/k as an algebraic extension of a purely transcendental extension (axiom of choice), reduce to purely transcendental case, view A_K as localization of A[{e_i}], and compare transcendence bases for function fields. Conceptual remark: equations with Q-coefficients give same dimension whether considered over Q or C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most hypersurfaces contain no lines (Exercises 12.2.N & 12.3.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: For d > 3 (over algebraically closed k), most degree-d surfaces in P^3 contain no lines; more precisely: all closed points of a nonempty Zariski-open subset of the parameter space correspond to surfaces containing no lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct an incidence correspondence X = {(ℓ,H): ℓ a line in P^3 contained in hypersurface H} ⊂ G(1,3) × parameter_space; show X is a bundle over G(1,3) and compute dim X = (d+3 choose 3)−1 −(d+1)+4, deduce image lies in a proper closed subset. Generalizes: if d > 2n−3 then most degree d hypersurfaces in P^n have no lines. Use dimension counts and incidence varieties; see related remarks on degree 1,2,3 cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Krull's Principal Ideal Theorem (geometric and algebraic versions, 12.3.2 & 12.3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Geometric: If X is locally Noetherian and f a function, the irreducible components of V(f) have codimension 0 or 1. Algebraic: If A is Noetherian and f ∈ A, then every prime p minimal among those containing f has codimension at most 1; if furthermore f is not a zero divisor, every such p has codimension exactly 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequence: locally principal closed subschemes have codimension 0 or 1, effective Cartier divisors have pure codimension 1. The algebraic statement is the fundamental technical tool used repeatedly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof technique via symbolic powers and Nakayama (12.3.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Method used in the proof of Krull's Principal Ideal Theorem: localize at a maximal ideal p minimal over (f), define q(n) = φ^{-1}(q^n A_q) (symbolic powers), show the sequence stabilizes modulo f and use Nakayama's Lemma to deduce q^n A_q = 0, hence Aq has dimension 0, contradicting assumptions unless codimension ≤ 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key steps: reduce to local ring, consider descending sequence q(n), use stabilization in A/(f) (Noetherian local ring property), apply Nakayama's Lemma twice. The construction of q(n) is highlighted as an instructive idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypersurfaces meet projective subvarieties (Important Exercise 12.3.C parts (a)-(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) If X ⊂ P^n_k has dimension ≥ 1 and H is a nonempty hypersurface in P^n_k, then H meets X. (b) If X has dimension r, any codimension-r linear space meets X. (c) There exists an intersection of r+1 nonempty hypersurfaces missing X. (d) If k is infinite, there exists an intersection of r hyperplanes meeting X in finitely many points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints: use the affine cone over H containing the origin and apply Krull's Principal Ideal Theorem to the cone over X; refine arguments for (b); construct hypersurfaces by induction on generic points for (c); for (d) use density over infinite fields and later relate the number of points to degree (Exercise 18.6.M).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bound on codimension of intersections in A^d (Exercise 12.3.E)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X and Y are irreducible closed subvarieties of codimensions m and n in A^d_k, then every component of X ∩ Y has codimension at most m + n in A^d_k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach: identify intersection with intersection of X×A^d and A^d×Y inside A^d×A^d, use diagonal ∆ as regular embedding of codimension d, and apply Krull's Principal Ideal Theorem and Exercise 12.2.F. Irreducibility hypothesis can be relaxed to equidimensionality with suitable generalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invertibility criterion in Noetherian rings (Exercise 12.3.G)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is an element of a Noetherian ring A that is contained in no codimension 0 or 1 prime ideals, then f is invertible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: if a function vanishes nowhere, it is invertible (refer to Exercise 4.3.F(b)). Use Krull-type reasoning about primes containing f.

rubrics_metrics.name: UFD characterization via codimension-1 primes (Proposition 12.3.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a Noetherian integral domain A, A is a unique factorization domain if and only if every codimension-1 prime ideal is principal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One direction follows from earlier lemma that UFD ⇒ codim-1 primes principal. Conversely, if codim-1 primes are principal, deduce existence and uniqueness of factorization: codimension-1 primes correspond to prime elements (unique up to units), prime elements are irreducible, and standard arguments give UFD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Krull's Height Theorem (12.3.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X = Spec A with A Noetherian and Z is an irreducible component of V(r1,...,r_ℓ) (r_i ∈ A), then codim Z ≤ ℓ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduction to the Noetherian local case and use of Lemma 12.3.9; height is another term for codimension. This gives a bound on how many equations can cut out a component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systems of parameters and finite dimension of Noetherian local rings (12.3.J & 12.3.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) If (A,m) is Noetherian local and there exist g1,...,g_ℓ with V(g1,...,g_ℓ) = {[m]}, then dim A ≤ ℓ, so Noetherian local rings have finite dimension. (b) If d = dim A, there exist g1,...,g_d ∈ A with V(g1,...,g_d) = {[m]}. Such a sequence is called a system of parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Krull's Height Theorem to get the inequalities; geometric translation: a d-dimensional germ can be cut out set-theoretically by d equations, and always need at least d.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedding-dimension bound (Theorem 12.3.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any Noetherian local ring (A,m,k), dim A ≤ dim_k m/m^2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: choose a k-basis of m/m^2, lift to elements f1,...,fn of m; Nakayama's Lemma shows (f1,...,fn) = m, then apply system-of-parameters result to conclude dim A ≤ n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algebraic Hartogs's Lemma (12.3.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is an integrally closed Noetherian integral domain, then A = ⋂_{p codimension 1} A_p (intersection inside the field of fractions K(A)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric reading: a rational function on a Noetherian normal scheme with no poles at codimension-1 points is regular. Proof uses the ideal of denominators I of x, choose minimal prime q over I, localize at q, construct z = yx with y chosen so that I ⊃ q^{n−1}, then split into two cases leading to contradictions unless x ∈ A. Compare to Serre's criterion for normality and valuation ring characterization of integral closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codimension pathology example (12.3.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: A = k[x](x)[t] (polynomials in t with coefficients rational functions of x with no x in denominator). Then xt − 1 generates a maximal ideal of codimension 1 whose quotient is a field (dimension 0), but A itself has dimension at least 2. Thus there is a codimension-1 prime in a 2-dimensional ring whose quotient is dimension 0 (pathology of codimension notion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Picture Spec A as a germ to visualize how V(xt−1) doesn't meet V(x) and cannot specialize to it; used to warn that codimension can behave oddly in non-finite-type contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lines on hypersurfaces (part 2, Exercise 12.3.K)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f(x0,...,xn) = f_d(x1,...,xn) + x0 f_{d-1}(x1,...,xn) + ... + x0^{d-1} f_1(x1,...,xn) is homogeneous degree d cutting out X with p = [1,0,...,0], then there is a line through p contained in X iff f_1 = f_2 = ... = f_{n-1} = 0 have a common zero in P^{n-1}. For d ≤ n−1, for most hypersurfaces X of degree d in P^n most points p ∈ X have no lines through them contained in X, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use earlier Exercise 12.3.C(a) for part of the argument. Part (c) suggests using Chevalley's theorem to spread 'there exists p in X with no line through it' to a dense open condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codimension inequality for morphisms (Key Exercise 12.4.A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose π : X → Y is a morphism of locally Noetherian schemes and p ∈ X with q = π(p). Then codim_X p ≤ codim_Y q + codim_{π^{-1}(q)} p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: take a system of parameters for q in Y and a system of parameters for p in the fiber π^{-1}(q), use them to find codim_Y q + codim_{π^{-1}(q)} p elements of O_{X,p} cutting out p in Spec O_{X,p}. This aligns with geometric intuition that fiber codimensions add up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic fiber dimension theorem (Theorem 12.4.1 and Corollary 12.4.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is a finitely presented dominant morphism of irreducible schemes with trdeg K(X)/K(Y) = r, then there exists a nonempty open U ⊂ Y such that for all q ∈ U, the fiber over q has pure dimension r (or is empty). For π : X → Y a morphism of irreducible k-varieties with dim X = m and dim Y = n, there is a nonempty open U so fibers over U have pure dimension m−n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof outline: reduce to affine case, consider generic fiber A ⊗_B K(B), apply Noether normalization to obtain t1,...,tr algebraically independent with A ⊗_B K(B) integral over K(B)[t1,...,tr]; clear denominators to get ti ∈ A over an open D(b), then Spec A_b finite surjective over Spec B_b[t1,...,tr], deduce fiber dimensions via Exercise 12.4.A and finiteness. Idea: spread-out argument from the generic point using finitely many denominators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for irreducibility via proper morphism (Exercise 12.4.D)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is a proper morphism to an irreducible variety Y and all fibers of π are nonempty, irreducible, and of the same dimension, then X is irreducible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the properness and fiber irreducibility & dimension constancy to deduce connectedness and irreducibility of total space (exercise suggests applying previous fiber dimension results).

rubrics_metrics.name: Upper semicontinuity of fiber dimension (Theorem 12.4.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) For π : X → Y a finite type k-morphism, the function p ↦ (dimension of the fiber component of π^{-1}(π(p)) containing p) is upper semicontinuous on X. (b) If furthermore π is closed (e.g., proper), then the function q ↦ (dimension of π^{-1}(q)) is upper semicontinuous on Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof idea for (a): define F_n = {points where fiber-dimension ≥ n}, show F_n closed by induction on dim Y (base dim Y = 0 trivial), use Exercise 12.4.A to control relative dimension r = dim X − dim Y; for closedness on target in (b) require π closed (counterexamples exist if closedness dropped).
